name: addpipe16_carryselect8_8
rationale: All three prior explicit gate-level restructurings (Kogge-Stone, mux-based conditional-sum, 4-bit CLA) underperformed the plain '+' baseline, indicating that Yosys/ABC's native '+' synthesis already produces highly-optimized adder mappings that hand-coded gate networks fail to beat. Rather than fighting the tool's own adder inference, this design keeps two independent native '+' operations (an 8-bit lower add and two speculative 8-bit upper adds for cin=0/cin=1) and only adds a single 8-bit mux selected by the lower carry-out. This halves the effective carry-propagation depth seen by the synthesizer (8-bit chains instead of 16-bit) while letting ABC fully optimize each small '+' the way it already does for the winning (16,) baseline, and only adds one mux level of overhead versus the monolithic add. This is a genuinely different strategy (native-adder carry-select rather than hand-built prefix/mux/CLA networks) and is a plausible way to beat the current best WNS at a modest, bounded area cost (roughly one extra 8-bit adder + 8 muxes versus full 16-bit duplication).
